chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Baseer: If you fear a matter taking place or a need which you require, so begin with Allah and glorify Him and extol upon Him just as He is rightful of it, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and ask your need, and try to cry and even if it (the teardrop) is like the head of the fly.
Indeed, my father (peace be upon him) was saying: The closest of what the servant can be from the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is when performing prostration and while he is weeping.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for supplication to ensure closeness to God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a specific supplicatory protocol for Abu Baseer, emphasizing that initiating with divine glorification and prophetic blessings, followed by humble weeping, maximizes the likelihood of acceptance. This practice is rooted in the tradition of Imam al-Baqir, who identified the state of prostration combined with tears as the moment when the servant is closest to God, highlighting the spiritual efficacy of emotional humility in Shia devotional life. The emphasis on even minimal weeping ('like the size of a fly') underscores that the sincerity of the heart matters more than the volume of tears, a concept deeply valued in Shia jurisprudence of supplication.
